correctness.rationale: For complex continuous f on the normalized 2π circle, sharp convolution operator norm equals normalized L1 of the continuous kernel. The fixed perturbation gap is bounded pointwise by |h|, avoiding false singular domination at t=0. Uniform angular trigonometric approximation away from t=0 and the Riemann–Lebesgue lemma yield the phase-average limit, followed by ε→0. Paired phases u and u+π give nonnegative and strictly positive angular cost on each open set where h≠0; h_F is nonzero. Explicit angular splitting for h=1 reduces to (2/π)(t/2−tan(t/4)) on (0,π), integrating to 1/2−4 log2/π². Independent quadrature n=32,128,512 gave gaps 0.2036470,0.2151803,0.2180814 versus 0.2190780289, corroboration only.
